latest_session.goal: Finish the EliteBook crash diagnosis. The 15:41 session copied the dumps and installed WinDbg but the machine crashed mid-analysis (16:04); this session resumed from the files on disk in an elevated window.
latest_session.outcome: Root cause found and the driver removed. Connecting to `vpn.dtu.dk` (16:18) did not upgrade the client: the headend offers only AnyConnect 4.5.03040, so the downloader skipped it. VPN last used 2026-01-27. Cisco Secure Client 5.1.3.62 was therefore uninstalled silently (`msiexec /X{5AE2D1E5-CA9D-4B56-BF01-178F7E2C0033} /qn`, exit 0, log in `Desktop\minidumps\cisco_uninstall.log`); the `acsock` service key and `vpnva64-6.sys` are gone, the orphan `acsock64.sys` file remains because the auto-mode guard refuses delete and rename in `System32\drivers`; the user deleted it by hand from the admin prompt afterwards. Original finding: All six crashes are 0xD1 in the UDP receive path. Five (09-16 x4, 09-17) bucket as `AV_tcpip!INET_UNALIGNED_ADDR_EQUAL` (invalid endpoint read in `UdpDeliverDatagrams` on the NDIS receive thread); the sixth (09-18 16:04) faults directly in `acsock64.sys+0x2ab6e` (`AV_acsock64!unknown_function`, NULL read at IRQL 2, process svchost) and Windows' Event 1001 names acsock64.sys too. `acsock64.sys` is the Cisco Secure Client WFP socket interceptor, v5.1.2.22 built 2023-12-21, loaded in every dump; the installed client is 5.1.3.62 (2026-01-21). The 09-11 cumulative update KB5124008 replaced `tcpip.sys`/`ndis.sys`; crashes started 09-16; KB5129241 (09-17) did not help. Trigger explained: Teams (WebView2, crash 2 was in `msedgewebview2.exe`) and browsers (QUIC) flood UDP at launch. Realtek audio and BIOS are cleared. WinDbg is installed per-user as MSIX; `cdbX64.exe` is on the WindowsApps alias path and works headless with `-z <dmp> -y srv*<cache>*https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols -c "!analyze -v; q"`. The first run per machine is slow because `lm t n` pulls every module image from the symbol server; later runs use the cache.
